FortiOS 5.2 has no DNS protocol setting (CLI Reference 5.2 p. 495): DNS is always cleartext. The 8.0 CLI default is also cleartext; it is written explicitly so the result does not depend on how the factory configuration of the target sets it.
5.2 uses a numeric time zone index; 8.0 expects a time zone database name (e.g. Europe/Rome). No official table maps one to the other: set it by hand.
Default disable in 5.2 (CLI Reference 5.2 p. 157), enable in 8.0. Written explicitly on deny policies so they keep not matching traffic to virtual IPs.

FortiOS 5.2 has no server-identity-check setting (CLI Reference 5.2, user ldap, pp. 723-725); 8.0 checks the server certificate name by default. Written as disable to keep the 5.2 behaviour (to confirm in the lab); enable it once the server certificate matches.

Default disable in 5.2 (CLI Reference 5.2 p. 552: get the gateway from the DHCP or PPPoE server), enable in 8.0 (distance 5). Written explicitly so that a DHCP/PPPoE port does not take the default route from the static WAN. To confirm in the lab.
Distance of the learned default route: 1 in 5.2 (CLI Reference 5.2 p. 553), 5 in 8.0. Written when the source takes the gateway from DHCP/PPPoE.
5.2 takes a bare address (remote-ip <ipv4>, CLI Reference 5.2 p. 561); 8.0 takes address and mask (ipv4-classnet-host). The host mask is written explicitly so the remote end stays a single address.
NAT traversal keepalive: 5 seconds in 5.2 (CLI Reference 5.2 p. 789), 10 in 8.0. Written explicitly when NAT traversal is enabled.
